Hi Emma / Tom,

Thanks again for the briefing last week — appreciate the clarity on your batch inference load and the need for predictable throughput for model inference at peak. Attached is our initial Dedicated Pricing Proposal (Dedicated_Pricing_Proposal_Solace_v1.pdf) and a short note that sketches two commit options.

High level asks from our side so we can tighten pricing:
- Can you confirm expected steady-state tokens/sec and worst-case burst window (minutes)?
- Do you have an internal limit on per-request sequence length we should use for SLO modeling?
- Any regulatory constraints that would force private deployment vs our hosted/dedicated blend?

1) Reserved pool (monthly commit) — fixed CU commitment, predictable throughput, lower unit price.
2) Commit + burst credits — smaller baseline commit + priced burst capacity; slightly higher unit price but more flexibility.

I flagged the sections we'll want to align on contract language: definition of a Capacity Unit (CU), the throughput guarantees (p95 latency targets and per-minute TPS), and the service credit ladder for shortfalls.

Folks —

Draft language and pricing framework below. I attached a simple workbook (Capacity_Defs_v1.xlsx) mapping CU to measurable metrics.

Proposed deterministic CU definition (redline-ready):
"Capacity Unit (CU) means one GPU-hour measured on a 32 GB usable VRAM instance, where a GPU-hour equals one hour of allocated GPU time on a single inference device. For multi-GPU allocations, CU is calculated as the sum of individual GPU-hours across devices. A CU is considered consumed when Redwood schedules and starts work measurable against the customer's commit; idle preallocated time is not billed as CU unless used to serve inference traffic."

Throughput guarantees mapping:
- We will guarantee a baseline throughput measured as CUs per calendar month tied to the committed pool.
- For latency SLOs, define per-request p95 computed across requests served from the committed pool. Where latency shortfalls occur, credits will be applied per the service credit ladder below.

Service credit ladder (example):
- <99.5% monthly committed throughput fulfilled: 5% credit to monthly committed fees
- <98.0%: 10% credit
- <95.0% or repeated incidents (3+ in 90 days): 20% credit + remediation plan

Discount tiers (three tiers based on monthly CU commit):
- Tier A: 1–5k CU / month — baseline list price
- Tier B: 5k–20k CU / month — 18% discount on token-equivalent unit price; 6% amortized implementation credit applied over first 3 months
- Tier C: 20k+ CU / month — 30% discount; 12% amortized implementation credit over first 6 months + one-time migration credit

Notes:
- Define CU amortization for upfront payments in the contract (we amortize credits monthly).
- For burst: we recommend explicit priced burst pool; bursts consumed on top of committed CU bill at a higher rate but do not affect committed pool SLAs unless the committed pool is exhausted.

Attach: Capacity_Defs_v1.xlsx

LMK if you want the legal redline. I can draft a replacement clause for Section 3 (Definitions) + Section 5 (Service Levels).

-Aditya
